**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — T4C Termination for convenience**

**What I found**

| Direction | Position | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Counterparty (Cellco as Servicer) | §7.1 "No Resignation" — may not resign unless legally unable to perform; §7.3 requires continued performance until a Successor Servicer accepts | **Exceeds preferred** — no Vendor convenience right at all |
| Our party (Issuer/Depositor) | §7.2 removal requires a Servicer Termination Event, and the trigger is pulled by the Indenture Trustee at Controlling Class direction — not by us; §8.3 otherwise runs to the last Receivable | **Fails fallback** — no convenience right whatsoever |

A full-text search for "convenience" returns only the headings clause at §10.10, and "without cause" returns nothing — confirming the absence is real, not buried elsewhere. The term plainly exceeds 12 months. Per the detection guidance this is a *deviation (missing behaviour)* rather than a `missing` finding, since a usable termination architecture (Articles VII–VIII) exists.

**Redline (validated ok:true)** — new §7.1A inserted after p0316: Issuer, at the Depositor's direction, may terminate the Servicer for convenience on **30 days' notice**, with **no fee, penalty or make-whole**, plus refund of prepaid Servicing Fees, expressly plugged into the existing §§7.3–7.5 transition machinery so noteholder servicing continuity is preserved. The 60–90 day fallback is offered in the comment.

**Judgment calls worth flagging to you**

1. *I did not redline §7.1 or §7.3.* These bind the counterparty and benefit us — flagging them would be backwards.
2. *I deliberately did not double-flag the 10-day Optional Redemption notice.* §§8.1–8.2 vest the exit in the "Class A Certificateholder," which p0668 defines as "the Originators or their designee" — i.e. the counterparty side — on only ten days' notice, which on a literal reading looks like walk-away territory. I treated it as noted-not-flagged because it is not service abandonment: the price must be "as agreed upon by the Class A Certificateholder and the Issuer" (a genuine Issuer veto), and exercise requires the Notes, accrued interest, Make-Whole Payments and all other Issuer obligations to be paid in full. Economically it pays our stakeholders out rather than stranding us. **If your house view is that any counterparty-side unwind on sub-90-day notice must be papered, this is the one to revisit** — it would be a second op extending §8.2(b) notice to 90 days.
3. Confidence 0.72. The genuine uncertainty is structural, not textual: in a rated securitization, an at-will Issuer right to fire the Servicer is unusual and rating agencies and noteholders may resist it, which is why I conditioned it on the §7.4 Successor Servicer mechanics (the Indenture Trustee must promptly engage a successor, with automatic fallback to itself, so the right is not illusory). Expect the fallback, or a successor-appointment condition, to be where this lands.
